author: François Rochon
title: Giverny Capital Annual Letter to our Partners 2025
headline: François Rochon after a weak 2025 (+2.7% vs 13.7%): he sold CarMax and Fiserv, keeps Constellation and warns AI spending rhymes with the railways.
summary: The Rochon Global Portfolio returned 2.7% in 2025 against 13.7% for its benchmark, though it has compounded at 14.7% a year since 1993. Rochon explains rather than excuses: CarMax and Fiserv both fell more than 50% and were sold, and Constellation Software, the largest holding, dropped 26% on fears that AI will replace software, even as its earnings per share rose 21%. He estimates his companies’ intrinsic value grew about 13%. On AI he sees a real revolution but circular deals and short-lived GPUs, and recalls that railways and fiber optics rarely paid off for early investors. Gold and Bitcoin he dismisses as assets without intrinsic value.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: Sold CarMax after 18 years as Carvana and dealers took share, and Fiserv after its CEO left for government; both fell more than 50% in 2025.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: Constellation Software is less threatened by AI than feared: revenue grew 15% and adjusted EPS 21%, and cheaper acquisition targets may even help. He keeps the shares.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: AI is a revolution, but deals that loop money from Nvidia to OpenAI to Oracle and back are hard to value, and GPUs stay competitive for only three to five years.

takeaways.label: Watch
takeaways.text: The ten largest S&P 500 stocks trade at about 28 times next year’s earnings, the other 490 at about 19 times.

risks.text: Companies with little revenue are borrowing tens of billions for AI data centers whose GPUs may be obsolete in five years.
The S&P 500 trades at 25 times earnings against a median of about 18 since 1996; at 18 it would be 28% lower.
Wall Street sells software, information-services and even engineering stocks first on AI fears and checks the facts later.

quotes.text: Wall Street's typical approach is to sell first and examine the facts later.
quotes.context: On the AI selloff in software

quotes.text: it seems unrealistic to believe that an operator of a dozen mini-golf courses is going to start coding their own AI-powered reservation software to save something like $5,000 in annual fees!
history has repeatedly shown that this type of investment is rarely, on the whole, profitable for early investors.
